titles.text: Closing My Company Taught Me How to Learn with AI
titles.why: A real story with a twist: an ending that became a lesson. Concrete enough to be believable, broad enough for anyone facing change. No outcome promised.

titles.text: AI Was My Tutor When My Company Closed
titles.why: Short and personal (38 characters, never cut off). The phrase 'AI was my tutor' is the film's idea in four words. Pairs with Thumbnail A.

titles.text: How I Taught Myself a Whole New Process with AI
titles.why: A clear how-to promise for people who search for learning with AI. Less emotional than the story titles.

titles.text: Facing a Big Change? Learn It with AI
titles.why: Opens with the viewer's own question, so it speaks to the widest audience. Vaguer about what the video shows. Pairs with Thumbnail D.

titles.text: Learn Anything with AI: My Real Test (Part 1)
titles.why: Bold promise, then grounds it in a real test. 'Anything' is a stretch: the film shows one process, so this one leans most on hype.

descriptionTemplate:
Every big change starts with something you don't know yet. Mine was closing my own UK company, and I used AI as my tutor to learn the whole process.

This is Part 1 of 3: how to teach yourself something completely new with AI, using a real company liquidation as the example.

In this video:
• Five steps to learn anything new, with AI as a tutor (not a lawyer)
• Plain-English explanations: IR35, HMRC, insolvency practitioners, MCP, n8n and AI agents
• What it cost and how long it took
• The honest part: what AI can't do, and why the professional decides
• Three lessons from my inbox
• Workflows plus AI agents, and why I share the real journey

thumbnailRules: Six words or fewer, large enough to read at 168 x 94 pixels.
All text is HTML in Inter (the film's font, SIL OFL, files in thumbnails/fonts/), never AI-drawn.
The film's look: black, white, one blue accent, the same drawings as the video.
No figures, no names, no personal data, no fake documents.
Do not promise an outcome (no 'fixed', 'solved' or 'guaranteed').
With a clear photo of your face on the clear side, a thumbnail usually does better: expression matters more than polish.
